key_concepts: Typhoons begin from tropical thunderstorms that gather ocean moisture through strong winds
Earth's rotation makes the developing storm spin
Heat released from moisture draws more air toward the storm center and drives evaporation
Heat and air flowing toward the eye complete typhoon formation
The eye of a typhoon is calm
The eyewall has the highest wind speeds and most intense weather
PAGASA uses a five-level Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal system based on wind speed
Tropical cyclone categories range from tropical depression to super typhoon with increasin
Landmasses such as the Sierra Madre mountain range weaken typhoons and reduce their impact
Warm ocean water and storm surges strengthen typhoons and increase coastal impacts
The Philippines experiences an average of 20 tropical cyclones each year
